identity.name: Vasa
identity.botanical_name: Adhatoda vasica Nees (syn. Justicia adhatoda L.)

classification.habit: Dense evergreen shrub, 1–3 m tall, with opposite leaves.
classification.habitat: Waste lands, roadsides, hedges and lower hill slopes; often grown as a hedge.
classification.distribution: Throughout India in the plains and up to about 1,300 m in the Himalaya.

identification.description: Broad lanceolate leaves with prominent pinnate venation and white two-lipped flowers resembling a lion mouth.
identification.whole_plant: Gregarious shrub with many ascending branches, large opposite lanceolate leaves and dense spikes of white two-lipped flowers.
identification.root: Woody taproot with yellowish-brown bark, bitter in taste.
identification.stem: Woody, branched stem; young branches green and pubescent, older ones with smooth light-brown bark.
identification.leaf: Leaves 10–30 cm long, 3–10 cm broad, lanceolate to ovate-lanceolate, slightly acuminate, base tapering, petiole 2–8 cm, exstipulate, 8–10 pairs of lateral veins; dried leaves dull brown above, greyish-brown below; characteristic odour; bitter taste (API).
identification.flower: White, two-lipped flowers with purple or red-barred lower lip, in dense axillary spikes with large ovate bracts.
identification.fruit: Club-shaped, pubescent capsule about 2 cm long, opening by two valves.
identification.seed: Usually four rounded, tubercled seeds per capsule.
identification_points: Large lanceolate leaves with tapering base
Dense spikes of white two-lipped flowers with large bracts

therapeutics.dose: Patra swarasa 10–20 ml; Mula kwatha 40–80 ml; Pushpa swarasa 10–20 ml
therapeutics.anupana: Madhu (honey), especially with Vasa swarasa in Kasa and Raktapitta
therapeutics.precautions: Generally well tolerated in usual doses; the alkaloid vasicine has uterotonic (oxytocic) activity, so avoid in pregnancy. Large doses of swarasa may cause nausea and vomiting.
therapeutics.contraindications: Pregnancy; caution in Vata-predominant dry cough and in very weak patients because the drug is Ruksha and Sheeta.

phytochemistry.chemical_notes: The leaves contain quinazoline alkaloids, chiefly vasicine and vasicinone (API: alkaloids and essential oil); bromhexine and ambroxol are synthetic analogues of vasicine.

modern_information.evidence_summary: Adhatoda vasica for cough, bleeding and Pitta conditions.
recognized_uses: Bleeding disorders such as epistaxis and haemoptysis (traditional)
Source molecule for the mucolytic bromhexine
modern_information.safety_notes: Usually well tolerated at recommended doses; avoid in pregnancy because of the uterotonic action of vasicine.
